target_customer: Saudi retail consumers who want spending insight and automated, Sharia-compliant investing; later also companies via Drahim Business
problem: Individuals in Saudi Arabia had no single place to see all bank accounts and spending, and no simple way to turn spare cash into investments.
business_model: Fee on assets under management (0.25 percent per year stated on the company site) on top of a free personal finance management app; Drahim Business for companies
product_category: Personal finance management app with robo-advisory investing

founders.name: Sultan Alkhayal
previous_startups: Software development agency that built products for 20+ enterprise customers (per YC page; outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: Education not found in opened sources. Role CEO per Crunchbase listing seen in search results.

founders.name: Yasser Alshurihi
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no background. Crunchbase snippet calls him CFO; not opened.

competitors.name: Abyan Capital
competitors.what: CMA-licensed Saudi robo-advisor focused on long-term savings and retirement

competitors.name: Mint and Truebill
competitors.what: US personal finance apps used as the reference point in a Drahim user testimonial

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed bank data aggregation in Saudi Arabia before open banking was licensed, transaction categorization and licensed investment execution; the company later partnered with Alpaca for brokerage rails.

defensibility.rationale: SAMA and Capital Market Authority sandbox and licenses, plus a Sharia board, are slow for rivals to replicate; the app itself is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Al Rajhi Bank bought 65 percent in September 2024 and powers its own retail app with the Drahim PFM, so a bank absorbed it by investment rather than copying it.

market_need_then: Rising Saudi smartphone banking, Vision 2030 push for household savings and capital market participation, and a regulator creating fintech sandboxes. Pain stated by the company is lack of consolidated spending insight.

branding.name_origin: YC page says Drahim is Arabic slang for money, from the ancient Greek drachma.

identity.logo: No source describing the logo was found
identity.visual_style: Company site stresses design and animations via testimonials
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly colloquial Saudi Arabic positioning as your financial friend

branding.brand_signature: Arabic money slang as the name with a friendly tone

brand_strength.rationale: Locally resonant Arabic name and a 4.6 App Store rating claimed on the company site; no independent press on the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Drahim launched a Saudi personal finance and robo-advisory app, joined YC in Summer 2022, and won licenses from SAMA and the Capital Market Authority. Al Rajhi Bank acquired 65 percent in September 2024, which the bank's own release confirms, so the outcome is a majority acquisition by a strategic bank rather than a failure. Regulatory licensing and local fit were the main assets.
notes: Unverified funding: aggregators (CB Insights, Seedtable, a profile page) report about 500K USD seed in 2022 from YC, 500 Global and Sanabil, with conflicting dates and investor lists; not recorded as a round. Seedtable lists a deal value of 22.2M USD, unverified; the bank did not disclose a price. One aggregator says June 2024 for the acquisition; the bank's own materials say September 2024. Directory status is Active with a majority stake held by Al Rajhi. Competitor pages were seen as search results, not opened, and are undated, so the years are founding years. Co-founder education not found.
